subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the trust lifecycle for host-read generated HTML after outbound staging?
rationale: The code looks correct, but the permanent security boundary is a maintainer-owned choice because it authorizes a new trusted path for local HTML delivery.

options.title: Accept provenance-gated staging
options.body: Merge after security/area ownership accepts that staged HTML is trusted only when it was marked from a previously trusted source and the delivered bytes match sha256 and size.

options.title: Tighten before merge
options.body: Ask for additional lifecycle constraints such as TTL pruning or narrower re-staging semantics before accepting the boundary.

options.title: Replace the design
options.body: Pause this PR and request a different owner-approved trust mechanism if SQLite provenance is not the desired permanent contract.

recommendation.title: Accept provenance-gated staging
recommendation.body: Merge after security/area ownership accepts that staged HTML is trusted only when it was marked from a previously trusted source and the delivered bytes match sha256 and size.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the original trusted generated HTML host-read seam and has the strongest feature-history connection to this boundary.
